slots.practicalActivity: Pick one centralized exchange feature (e.g. Coinbase's trading) and one DeFi equivalent (e.g. Uniswap) and write a short comparison of custody, trust assumptions, and failure modes for each.
slots.deliverable: A short comparison note: custodial vs. self-custodial for the same type of trade.

lessons.title: The Major Categories of DeFi Protocols

slots.practicalActivity: Visit DeFiLlama and find one real, currently-live protocol in each of four categories (AMM, lending, staking/yield, and a DAO treasury), noting its approximate TVL.
slots.deliverable: A table of four real protocols (name, category, approximate TVL) sourced from DeFiLlama.

slots.practicalActivity: Trace one real multi-protocol flow you can find documented (e.g. depositing into a lending protocol, then using the resulting receipt token as collateral elsewhere) and diagram the contracts it touches.
slots.deliverable: A simple diagram of one real composed DeFi flow across multiple protocols.

slots.practicalActivity: Pick a real deployed DeFi protocol's verified contract on Etherscan, open its 'Read Contract' tab, and call two real view functions (e.g. a pool's reserves or an exchange rate) to confirm they match the protocol's own UI.
slots.deliverable: Notes documenting two real on-chain values read directly from a verified contract, cross-checked against the protocol's UI.

slots.practicalActivity: Lab: using the protocol you picked in the previous lesson, write a one-page brief summarizing what it does, which category it belongs to, and one other protocol it composes with — your first 'read a real protocol' exercise for the course.
slots.deliverable: A one-page protocol brief grounded in real, verified on-chain data.

slots.practicalActivity: By hand (spreadsheet or calculator), compute the output amount for a swap against a constant-product pool given starting reserves and an input amount, using x·y=k.
slots.deliverable: A worked x·y=k calculation showing the exact output amount for a chosen swap.

slots.practicalActivity: Extend your spreadsheet from the previous lesson to compute how many LP tokens a new depositor would receive when adding liquidity proportionally to existing reserves.
slots.deliverable: An updated spreadsheet calculating LP token minting for a new deposit.

slots.practicalActivity: Using the same pool, model what happens to your LP position's value if the external price of one asset doubles, and compare it to simply holding both assets — i.e. calculate impermanent loss.
slots.deliverable: A spreadsheet row showing the impermanent-loss percentage for a 2x price move on your example pool.

slots.practicalActivity: Deploy the lesson's simplified `SimpleAMM` teaching contract to a local Hardhat/Foundry testnet, call `addLiquidity` then `swapAForB`, and confirm the output matches your hand calculation from earlier in this chapter.
slots.deliverable: A deployed-and-tested `SimpleAMM.sol` plus a test script confirming the swap output matches your spreadsheet math.

slots.practicalActivity: Look up a real Uniswap v3 pool on its analytics site and read off the current active tick range/price bounds for an existing position, contrasting it with the full-range liquidity you modeled earlier in this chapter.
slots.deliverable: Notes comparing a real Uniswap v3 concentrated position's price range to a full-range v2-style pool.

slots.practicalActivity: Lab: add a `removeLiquidity` function to your `SimpleAMM` contract that burns LP tokens and returns a proportional share of both reserves, and write a test proving a user who deposits then immediately withdraws gets back (approximately) what they put in.
slots.deliverable: An updated `SimpleAMM.sol` with a tested `removeLiquidity` function.

slots.practicalActivity: Lab: write a test suite for your `SimpleAMM` that runs a sequence of multiple swaps and liquidity changes from different accounts, asserting the constant-product invariant k never decreases except by the fee amount — your own mini invariant test.
slots.deliverable: A passing test suite asserting the x·y=k invariant holds (net of fees) across a multi-step scenario.

slots.practicalActivity: Using a real protocol's published collateral factor (e.g. look up Aave's or Compound's for ETH), calculate the maximum you could borrow against a $1,000 deposit.
slots.deliverable: A worked calculation of max borrow amount using a real protocol's actual collateral factor.

slots.practicalActivity: Look up a real lending market's current utilization rate and interest rate on a live dashboard (e.g. Aave's app), and plot by hand how the rate would change at 0%, 50%, and 95% utilization using the kinked-rate shape from the lesson.
slots.deliverable: A small spreadsheet chart of rate vs. utilization anchored to one real market's actual current numbers.

slots.practicalActivity: Using your overcollateralized-lending position from two lessons ago, calculate the price drop in the collateral asset that would push your health factor below 1, i.e. the exact liquidation price.
slots.deliverable: A calculated liquidation price for your example position.

slots.practicalActivity: Read a real public post-mortem or writeup of one flash-loan transaction (an arbitrage or a documented exploit) and trace, step by step, how the loan was borrowed and repaid within a single transaction.
slots.deliverable: A step-by-step trace of one real flash-loan transaction's borrow-act-repay sequence.

slots.practicalActivity: Deploy the lesson's teaching lending-pool contract locally, deposit collateral from one test account, borrow against it from another, and manually trigger the liquidation path by simulating a price drop.
slots.deliverable: A deployed lending-pool contract plus a test script exercising deposit, borrow, and a triggered liquidation.

slots.practicalActivity: Lab: add the interest-rate-model formula into your lending pool contract so borrow interest accrues based on utilization, and write a test showing accrued interest increases as utilization rises.
slots.deliverable: An updated lending pool contract with a utilization-based interest rate, verified by a passing test.

slots.practicalActivity: Lab: write an end-to-end test scenario on your lending pool — deposit, borrow near the limit, simulate a collateral price drop past the liquidation threshold, and confirm a liquidator account can successfully liquidate the position.
slots.deliverable: A passing end-to-end test proving your lending pool's full deposit-borrow-liquidate lifecycle works.

slots.practicalActivity: Look up a real protocol's staking contract (e.g. a token staking page) and note its lockup period and advertised reward rate.
slots.deliverable: Notes on one real protocol's actual staking terms (lockup period, reward rate).

slots.practicalActivity: Find one real yield-farm pair on a DEX's farms page and calculate its advertised APY from the reward-token emission rate and pool TVL, by hand.
slots.deliverable: A hand-calculated APY for one real live farm, checked against the platform's displayed number.

slots.practicalActivity: Model the difference between manually claiming and reinvesting rewards weekly versus an auto-compounding vault doing it continuously, over a 6-month period at a fixed APY, using a spreadsheet.
slots.deliverable: A spreadsheet comparing manual vs. auto-compounded returns over 6 months at the same APY.

slots.practicalActivity: Look up a real token's published emission schedule (e.g. a linear decay or halving schedule) and plot its weekly reward output over the first year.
slots.deliverable: A chart of one real token's actual emission schedule for its first year.

slots.practicalActivity: Lab: write a small Solidity staking contract (stake, accrue rewards per second, claim, unstake) and a test that fast-forwards time to confirm rewards accrue linearly, implementing this chapter's staking mechanics in code.
slots.deliverable: A tested staking contract with a passing time-fast-forward test proving linear reward accrual.

slots.practicalActivity: Lab: add an auto-compounding `compound()` function to your staking contract that reinvests accrued rewards back into the stake, and write a test comparing a position that calls `compound()` weekly against one that never does, over simulated time.
slots.deliverable: An updated staking contract with a tested auto-compound function showing a measurable return difference.

slots.practicalActivity: Compare two real tokens' supply models side by side — one fixed-cap (like Bitcoin) and one inflationary (pick a real DeFi governance token) — noting current vs. max supply for each.
slots.deliverable: A table comparing two real tokens' actual supply models.

slots.practicalActivity: Pick one real protocol's token and classify every real use case listed in its own docs (fee discount, voting, staking, etc.) as utility or governance.
slots.deliverable: A classified list of one real token's actual documented use cases.

slots.practicalActivity: Find one real project's published token-vesting schedule and compute how many tokens would be unlocked 6, 12, and 24 months from its start, given its cliff and linear-vest terms.
slots.deliverable: A computed unlock table (6/12/24 months) for one real project's actual vesting terms.

slots.practicalActivity: Critique a real protocol's incentive program (e.g. a liquidity mining campaign) you can find documented, identifying one way mercenary capital could exploit it per the lesson's framework.
slots.deliverable: A short written critique identifying a real incentive program's exploitable weak point.

slots.practicalActivity: Build a spreadsheet model projecting one hypothetical token's circulating supply over 24 months (combining this chapter's vesting unlocks and the previous chapter's emission schedule) against a basic demand assumption, and chart the resulting trend.
slots.deliverable: A 24-month supply/demand spreadsheet model with a chart showing the token's projected circulating-supply curve.

slots.practicalActivity: Lab: write a Solidity vesting contract implementing a cliff + linear release schedule, and a test that fast-forwards through the cliff and confirms zero tokens are claimable before it and the correct partial amount after.
slots.deliverable: A tested vesting contract proving correct cliff and linear-unlock behavior.

slots.practicalActivity: Lab: take your supply/demand spreadsheet model and add a second scenario with a 20% larger initial team allocation, comparing the two circulating-supply curves — your own sensitivity analysis on a tokenomics design choice.
slots.deliverable: An updated spreadsheet model with two compared tokenomics scenarios and a short written takeaway.

slots.practicalActivity: Find a real DAO's active or recently-closed on-chain proposal (e.g. on Tally or Snapshot) and read its exact quorum and voting-threshold requirements.
slots.deliverable: Notes on one real DAO proposal's actual quorum/threshold rules and current vote tally.

slots.practicalActivity: On that same DAO's governance app, look up how delegation works and find one real address that has delegated its voting power, noting the delegate and the amount.
slots.deliverable: Notes documenting one real delegation relationship found on a live governance app.

slots.practicalActivity: Look up a real DAO treasury's multisig on Etherscan (via a service like Safe), note its signer threshold (e.g. 5-of-9), and find one real executed transaction showing the timelock delay between proposal passing and execution.
slots.deliverable: Notes on a real multisig's signer threshold and one real timelock-delayed treasury transaction.

slots.practicalActivity: Deploy the lesson's simplified governance contract (propose, vote, execute after a timelock) locally, run a full proposal through it with multiple test-account votes, and confirm it reverts if executed before the timelock expires.
slots.deliverable: A deployed governance contract plus a test proving execution reverts before, and succeeds after, the timelock.

slots.practicalActivity: Lab: wire a simple ERC-20 governance token with balance checkpoints into your governance contract so voting power is read from real token balances at proposal-creation time, and test that a vote cast with zero tokens is rejected.
slots.deliverable: An integrated governance contract that checks real token-based voting power, verified by a passing test.

slots.practicalActivity: Open a real deployed NFT contract on Etherscan and compare its interface to a real ERC-1155 contract's, identifying the actual function signatures (`ownerOf` vs. `balanceOf(address,id)`) that distinguish them.
slots.deliverable: Notes comparing two real deployed contracts' actual ERC-721 vs. ERC-1155 function signatures.

slots.practicalActivity: Find one real protocol using NFTs as something other than art (e.g. Uniswap v3 LP positions as NFTs, or a real NFT-collateralized loan on a lending protocol) and trace what financial right the NFT actually represents.
slots.deliverable: A short writeup of one real non-collectible NFT use case and the right it encodes.

slots.practicalActivity: Look up a real NFT collection's royalty setting (e.g. via its marketplace listing or EIP-2981 implementation) and calculate the royalty payout on one real recent secondary sale.
slots.deliverable: A calculated royalty payout for one real, verifiable secondary NFT sale.

slots.practicalActivity: Review: write a short capstone brief tying this course together — pick one real DeFi protocol and describe which of its mechanics (AMM, lending, staking, tokenomics, governance, or NFT) you could now explain and partially reimplement in Solidity, citing the specific lesson/lab for each.
slots.deliverable: A capstone brief mapping one real protocol's mechanics back to the specific lessons/labs that taught them.

monthlyMilestoneContribution: After finishing this course, a student can read and reason about the math behind real DeFi protocols — pricing an AMM swap, modeling a lending pool's liquidation risk, designing a token's vesting and incentive schedule, and wiring up on-chain governance — and can point to working Solidity/JS code implementing each mechanic.
